title: PDL Week 9
coldOpen:
Game of the Week featured two winless teams combining for 106 points. Brian traded away the quarterback who would've won him a game, Greg left 57 points on his bench, and Mike hasn't won since we started discussing his undefeated season.

Welcome to Week 9 of the PDL Power Rankings.

1: I would like to formally apologize to everyone who spent the offseason telling me Delco wasn't a contender.
You were right. I was wrong.
You are handsome and have a beautiful personality. I am a fat piece of shit from Philly.

Lamar and Hurts are done for the year. Smitty has spent the entire season hurt, Tyler Warren is banged up while the Colts dismantle whatever remains of their franchise, and Josh Jacobs is a perfect microcosm for Delco: a dumpster fire of a person.
I don't even have a joke.
I am genuinely not having a good time.
Enjoy the rest of the rankings.
2: The PDL spent part of last week lobbying for Connecticut vs. Richmond to be named Game of the Week.
Two winless teams, one guaranteed to finally get a victory, and an opportunity to witness a little PDL history.
Jon won 76.28 to 30.08. And before anyone congratulates Richmond too enthusiastically, I want to put that into perspective.
Joe could've submitted his entire starting lineup TWICE and still lost by 16.12 points.
That's twenty players against ten. I'm genuinely impressed.
Not a single player in Connecticut's starting lineup scored six fantasy points.
TEN starters, and the leading scorer was Tanner McKee with 5.98.
Kaytron Allen, Reggie Virgil, and Ted Hurst all dropped a goose egg, while the entire starting receiving corps combined for 4.90 points.
That's the same amount Mason Taylor scored by himself, and he caught three passes for 19 yards.
I don't even know how you assemble a lineup that collectively avoids the end zone this effectively.
At some point, Joe has to be checking the waiver wire for players who accidentally scored a touchdown and making sure they're nowhere near his roster.

Richmond spent seven weeks waiting for the young players to develop, wondering whether the offense would ever produce enough to win a game, and Joe showed up with a lineup that made 76 points look like an offensive explosion.
So congratulations to Jon on finally getting into the win column. I'm sure we'll have plenty to discuss when we get to Richmond.
As for Joe, he's 0-8, his draft plans remain completely intact, and he has now successfully participated in the PDL's Game of the Week without providing a single highlight.
3: Jeff scored 145.28 points last week.
This week, he scored 145.42.
That's a difference of FOURTEEN HUNDREDTHS of a point, despite the fact that his entire starting receiving corps combined for two catches and 24 yards.
Talk about consistency.
Zay Flowers was targeted five times and caught absolutely nothing.
Tre Tucker, whom I spent last week praising as Jeff's most dependable receiver, followed that endorsement by also catching zero passes.
Jakobi Meyers managed two catches for 24 yards, giving Wichita a grand total of 3.40 fantasy points from THREE starting receivers.
Jeff still beat Brett by 36.82.
Fortunately, Joe Burrow apparently took one look at the receiving situation in Wichita and decided to personally handle the entire passing offense.
Burrow threw for 462 yards and five touchdowns against Tennessee, then ran in the game-winner in overtime.
He also threw THREE interceptions, all to the same defender.
Amani Hooker intercepted Joe Burrow three times in one afternoon and STILL lost.
Imagine having the best individual game of your professional career and the opposing quarterback finishes with six touchdowns.
Burrow scored 46.48 fantasy points.
Mahomes added another 31.44 against Denver, giving Jeff 77.92 points from his two quarterbacks alone.
That's more than half his team's entire production.
And Mahomes nearly had another touchdown.
With the Chiefs trailing Denver in the final seconds, Mahomes found Rashee Rice for what appeared to be the game-winning score as time expired.
Unfortunately, a false start wiped it away, and Mahomes was sacked on the final play.
Kansas City blew an 11-point fourth-quarter lead, lost its second consecutive game, and Jeff still walked away with 31 fantasy points from their quarterback.
The receiving situation is becoming worth watching, though. Davante Adams remains on IR, A.J. Brown is unavailable, and the trio Jeff started this week couldn't collectively produce a first down.
Keon Coleman Jr. actually had 12.10 points on the bench, and Courtland Sutton added another 7.30.
Jeff has spent months acquiring established veterans and somehow finds himself in November with a receiving room that might need a waiver-wire intervention.
Christian McCaffrey was also on bye, which makes another 145-point performance considerably more impressive.
James Cook continues to produce, Henry was serviceable, and Walker at least reached double digits.
Jeff has enough running backs to compensate for a disappointing week somewhere else, provided that somewhere else doesn't eventually become the entire receiving position.
Meanwhile, Tanish is also sitting at 7-1, having outscored Wichita by 1.42 points this week.

The defending champion is getting production from practically everywhere, and I suspect he'll be delighted to learn that Jeff just needed nearly 78 points from his quarterbacks to stay ahead of a 3-5 team.
Wichita remains #1, but the gap between Jeff and Tanish is getting increasingly difficult to justify.

Jeff still has the stronger overall scoring profile, and it's hard to argue with seven wins in eight weeks, especially when the roster is capable of producing this much while several key players are unavailable.

I just find it incredible that Jeff has spent the offseason assembling the most expensive collection of talent in the PDL, and we're entering November with Tre Tucker and Jakobi Meyers occupying two of his starting receiver spots.
Let's buckle up because the postseason continues to get closer.
We are officially in November Football time.
4: Max spent a good portion of October convincing us that Bryce Young had finally turned the corner.
I'm not sure what happened around that corner, but apparently there were six Green Bay defenders waiting to sack him.
Bryce finished Thursday night with 209 passing yards, an interception, and an 11.36-point performance that probably didn't warrant another emergency episode of the podcast.
Fortunately, C.J. Stroud was on bye, and Cam Ward decided this was the appropriate week to have the first 300-yard passing game of his NFL career.
Ward entered Sunday with four passing touchdowns through seven games.

He threw two against Cincinnati, added 41 rushing yards, converted two separate two-point attempts, and nearly pulled off an upset against a Bengals team that needed SIX touchdowns from Joe Burrow to win in overtime.
Tennessee is now 1-7, but Ward finished with 30.26 fantasy points for Max.
He's managed to become significantly more helpful to Murphy Street than he has been to the Tennessee Titans.
And then there's Michael Wilson, who was involved in one of the most ridiculous endings of the NFL weekend.
Arizona finally benched Jacoby Brissett against Dallas and brought in Gardner Minshew, who proceeded to lead the Cardinals back from a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit.
With six seconds remaining, Minshew found Wilson for the game-tying touchdown. Arizona then missed the extra point, because apparently winning a football game in regulation would've been too easy.
They eventually won in overtime, and Wilson finished with 111 receiving yards and a touchdown.
Ja'Marr Chase also had another monster afternoon, catching 11 passes for 141 yards against Tennessee.
Between Chase, Wilson and Ward, Max received 78.66 points from three players.
He needed every bit of that production because Jordan Mason contributed TWO points, Kyle Pitts finished with 2.60, and the running back situation remains fairly concerning.
But the bigger development is that Max finally had to beat someone other than Joe or Jon.
Greg was coming off a 158-point performance against Mike, and Murphy Street responded with 133.12 points of its own to improve to 6-2.
A much more convincing showing than the 89 points Max needed to beat Richmond last week.
I'm still hesitant to move him much higher.

The receiving depth is improving, and having Stroud, Young and Ward gives Max some legitimate options at quarterback, but this roster is awfully dependent on Chase and whatever production he can squeeze out of his running backs.
For now, Max is 6-2, has won four of his last five, and is getting productive performances from his players.
Meanwhile, I've spent all season worrying about his roster construction, and the only team he's lost to in the past five weeks is mine.
Which, given what has happened to Delco since, might be the most embarrassing result on Max's schedule.
5: After seven weeks of investing in the future, drafting rookies, and waiting for his young players to develop, Jon finally won a football game because he traded a 2028 fourth-round pick for 38-year-old Kirk Cousins.
If you don't like that, you don't like dynasty football.
On Friday afternoon, Brian shipped Cousins to Richmond for a fourth-round pick two years from now.
By Sunday, Cousins had thrown three touchdowns, rushed for another, and delivered 34.18 fantasy points in his Reavers debut.
Meanwhile, Brian lost his seventh game of the season.
Hollywood has apparently figured out how to help other teams win football games, which is encouraging progress for an organization that's still trying to figure out how to do it themselves.
And there's an even better wrinkle to this trade.
Remember Fernando Mendoza? The first overall pick in the NFL Draft? Jon owns him, too.
Las Vegas had lost four straight games, and the calls for Mendoza to replace Cousins were getting louder.
Klint Kubiak publicly backed his veteran quarterback, who responded by throwing three touchdowns against the Jets and leading the Raiders to a 38-33 victory.
Jon just acquired the quarterback who's actively preventing one of his prized rookies from getting on the field.
Every good Cousins performance makes Mendoza's debut a little less likely.

And after watching Cousins celebrate his rushing touchdown with a dance dedicated to the medical staff keeping his 38-year-old body functioning, I'm not convinced we're getting rid of this man anytime soon.
Kirk Cousins scored a touchdown and celebrated by thanking the people who work on his soft tissue.
Richmond's season was saved by a quarterback who has to acknowledge his physical therapists after running one yard.
As for the actual roster, the rookie development Jon was finally starting to enjoy took a bit of a vacation.
Omar Cooper followed up consecutive 100-yard performances by catching absolutely nothing against Las Vegas.
Makai Lemon and Antonio Williams were fine, but neither did anything particularly exciting.
Gunnar Helms actually had one of the better performances on Jon's roster with 14.60 points, which would've been useful had Jon not left him on the bench.
But who cares? Richmond finally won!
The Reavers finished with 76.28 points against Joe's 30.08, officially ending their seven-game losing streak.
Cousins alone outscored Connecticut's entire starting lineup, which tells you approximately everything you need to know about how competitive this matchup was.
Even if Jon hadn't traded for Cousins, his remaining nine starters would've scored 42.10 points.
He could've left the quarterback position completely empty and STILL beaten Joe by double digits.
Seven weeks without a win, six quarterbacks who couldn't complete a pass last week, and Jon finally makes the perfect emergency trade.
For the one opponent in the PDL he didn't actually need a quarterback to beat.
6: On Thursday, Brian traded Kirk Cousins to Jon for a 2028 fourth-round pick.
Three days later, Cousins scored 34.18 points for Richmond, Michael Penix scored NEGATIVE 5.90 for Hollywood, and Brian lost to Darren by 27.58.
Don't worry, I can do math and show my work:
If Brian had kept Cousins and started him over Penix, Hollywood would've won 180.00 to 167.50.
Instead, Jon got his first win of the season, Brian got his seventh loss, and somewhere in the distant future a fourth-round rookie will have the opportunity to make all of this worthwhile.
To appreciate just how spectacularly Penix ruined Brian's afternoon, Tampa Bay beat Atlanta 16-0 WITHOUT COMPLETING A SINGLE PASS.
Baker Mayfield went 0-for-3 and won an NFL game.
Penix completed eight passes to his own teammates and four to the Buccaneers.
His final passer rating was 12.0, which is genuinely impressive considering the NFL gives you a 39.6 just for throwing every pass directly into the ground.
And Penix was coming off a three-touchdown performance against San Francisco! Brian had every reason to feel comfortable starting him.
I'm not sure anybody could've anticipated Atlanta's offense producing fewer points than Joe's roster during the national anthem.
Tee Higgins went for 155 yards and two touchdowns. Tuten and Braelon Allen combined for 51.20 points, and Jordan Love added another 26.52.
Nico Collins was on bye, Egbuka was unavailable, and Brian STILL managed 139.92 points.
That would've beaten seven other teams in the PDL this week.
I spent last week questioning whether Hollywood could realistically make the playoffs, and I'm somehow less certain what to do with this team after its best performance in weeks.
Brian's offseason investments are beginning to produce, the younger running backs are contributing, and there's still enough talent here to put together some ridiculous scores.
Unfortunately, the PDL doesn't give you a participation trophy for assembling a theoretically competitive roster.
The points-based playoff spot has been the main thing in McFatty's mind.

And while I still think Hollywood has a chance to make things interesting, there's something deeply upsetting about watching a 1-7 owner score 140 points and knowing he could've won if he'd simply stayed put.
At least Hollywood got a 2029 4th.
7: I've spent the past several weeks trying to avoid giving this man any additional reasons to talk about his fantasy team, but after putting up a league-leading 167.50 points against Hollywood, I'm running out of excuses.
And he managed to do it with Matthew Stafford scoring 9.28 points against a Chargers team that hasn't won a football game all season.
The Rams won 24-9, but Stafford threw for 157 yards, one touchdown and an interception.
This is the same guy who was putting up 30-point performances earlier this season.
Fortunately, Darren has spent the past several years collecting enough talent that apparently he can afford to have his starting quarterback take the occasional Sunday afternoon off.
And Darren's running backs have been absolutely ridiculous.
Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 153 yards and a touchdown against the previously undefeated Vikings, handing Minnesota its first loss of the season.
Two weeks after Darren ended Jeff's undefeated streak, Gibbs helped end another one.
Then Monday Night Football happened.
Darren entered the evening trailing Hollywood by 19.84 points, with D'Andre Swift and Sam Darnold remaining.
Swift proceeded to score THREE rushing touchdowns against Seattle, despite averaging 2.6 yards per carry.
Twenty-seven carries, 69 yards, and three touchdowns.
Chicago apparently spent the entire second half marching down the field so Swift could collect another five-yard touchdown.
Darnold contributed another 20.52 points despite losing to the Bears, and Darren finished with nearly 28 more points than Brian.
I imagine Brian enjoyed watching his seventh loss develop over the course of a nationally televised football game.
And speaking of Brian, remember how he traded Kirk Cousins to Jon for a 2028 fourth?
Cousins threw TWO touchdowns to Brock Bowers this week.
The quarterback Brian traded away on Thursday helped Jon win his first game and spent Sunday feeding touchdowns to the tight end belonging to the guy Brian was facing.
Between Penix's four interceptions, Cousins' performance, and Bowers finishing with 28.20 points, Hollywood's quarterback management deserves its own episode of Hard Knocks.
What stands out about Darren's roster is how little he needed from some of his usual contributors.
Stafford was disappointing, CeeDee Lamb finished with 9.30, and Javonte Williams contributed 6.20.
Meanwhile, Golden continues to develop into a star, DJ Moore finally had a productive afternoon, and Darren had another 15 points from Luther Burden sitting on his bench.
He's now 5-3, and I'm considerably more impressed by how this roster has handled the past few weeks than I was earlier in the season.
The running backs have been outstanding, the tight ends are producing, and there's enough receiving talent that Darren doesn't need Lamb and Wilson to have monster games every Sunday.
Mike has now lost three consecutive games, Welch continues to climb, and Darren is making a claim for his 3rd title run.
8: Welch started both quarterbacks in the Cowboys-Cardinals game on Sunday. Somehow, BOTH of them managed to lose.
Dak Prescott watched Dallas blow a 14-point lead and lose 33-30 in overtime, while Jacoby Brissett was benched in the third quarter after throwing for 119 yards and an interception.
Gardner Minshew came in, threw three touchdowns, and led Arizona to its third victory of the season.
Brissett has since been demoted to the emergency third quarterback, behind rookie Carson Beck. I finally feel validated because of how trash I've been saying Brissett has been.
The best part is that Brissett losing his job actually HELPED Welch.
Minshew came in and immediately remembered that Trey McBride existed, eventually connecting with him for a fourth-quarter touchdown.
McBride finished with 20.20 points, while Brissett contributed 2.46.
I don't think I've ever seen a quarterback become more valuable to his fantasy owner by getting himself removed from an NFL game.
And Welch still beat Mike by 30 points.
That's now consecutive wins over Darren and Mike, two teams we've spent the entire season discussing as potential championship favorites.
Meanwhile, Dallas is 6-2, and I'm beginning to wonder how much longer we can keep talking about Welch as the guy trying to catch up to the contenders when he's actively beating them.
Amon-Ra St. Brown and Drake London combined for 10.40 points.

Prescott was fine, Brissett was a disaster, and one of his better running back performances came from Emmett Johnson, a rookie who has spent most of the season doing practically nothing in Kansas City.
Johnson entered Sunday having accumulated 144 receiving yards all season.
He caught five passes for 128 yards against Denver ALONE, including a 73-yard touchdown.
Kenneth Walker, whom Jeff acquired to help build the greatest collection of running backs since the 1985 Chicago Bears, finished with 69 rushing yards in the same game.
Apparently, Patrick Mahomes has decided the running back Jeff didn't acquire is the one who should be catching his passes.
Welch also has an absurd collection of tight ends.
McBride and Harold Fannin combined for 43.60 points, with Dallas Goedert adding another 7.20.
Fannin caught ten passes for 154 yards against Pittsburgh; TE premium is looking good in Dallas.
The quarterback situation still deserves some attention, though.
Kyler Murray scored 22.90 on the bench, Jared Goff is having an uneven stretch, and Brissett may not see the field again unless Arizona runs out of quarterbacks.
For a team seriously pursuing a championship, relying on that much uncertainty at the most important position is asking for trouble.
But Welch is putting himself in a pretty interesting position.
He's finished second in the PDL twice, and we've spent plenty of time making fun of his inability to get over that final hurdle.
Now he's beaten Darren and Mike in consecutive weeks, and neither game required some miraculous 40-point performance from Dak.
I was prepared to spend November questioning whether Dallas had enough firepower to compete with the top three.
Instead, Welch is making a pretty compelling argument that we should be questioning whether Mike and Darren have enough to compete with him.
And he's doing it while starting a quarterback whose actual NFL team has asked him to remain available only in the event of an emergency.
9: Greg could've started Tyler Allgeier this week and lost by 0.14 points.
I want everyone to appreciate how close we came to witnessing something genuinely devastating.
Allgeier rushed for 147 yards, caught five passes for another 44, and scored twice against Dallas.
He finished with 33.60 fantasy points on Greg's bench.
Had London started him over Emanuel Wilson, who contributed absolutely nothing, Max would've won 133.12 to 132.98.
I almost wish Greg had made that substitution.
A loss by fourteen hundredths of a point would've been considerably more entertaining than what we actually got.
Unfortunately, Greg also left Adonai Mitchell's 23.70 points on the bench too.
Mitchell caught seven passes for 142 yards and a touchdown against Las Vegas.
Geno was starting for London while the receiver responsible for a significant portion of his production was sitting on Greg's bench.
Had Greg started Allgeier and Mitchell over Wilson and Rashod Bateman, London would've scored 153.98 and beaten Max by more than 20 points.
That one is going to sting, but it's not like Greggy cares anymore.
And Allgeier's performance is particularly interesting considering what happened to Bijan Robinson.
Greg spent the offseason acquiring running backs, eventually assembled a backfield featuring Bijan and Quinshon Judkins, and watched those two combine for 13.50 points.
Meanwhile, Bijan's former backup in Atlanta was busy running all over Dallas in an Arizona uniform.
Greg had the best running back on his roster sitting behind the guy who used to be ahead of him on the depth chart. Apparently, old habits die hard.
I'm also trying to figure out what to make of London after last week.
Greg just embarrassed Mike with 158.16 points, temporarily making every criticism I've directed at his roster look ridiculous.
Seven days later, he's back under 100 and losing to Max.
Even Rome Odunze, the receiver Greg was willing to sacrifice Chris Olave to acquire, has yet to deliver the kind of consistent production that would make that trade any less painful to revisit.
The quarterbacks are actually doing their jobs.
Bo Nix and Geno Smith combined for 44.28 points, and Greg has enough talent scattered throughout this roster to produce another big week.
The problem is that he seems to have absolutely no idea when those performances are coming.
At 3-5, London is running out of opportunities to make these kinds of mistakes, especially after spending the first half of the season rearranging its roster.
I spent the past month questioning Greg's trades.
After looking at this week's bench, I'm beginning to think the trades were the part of running this team he was actually good at.
10: George Pickens was caught on video sprinting into the Cowboys locker room seconds after Arizona kicked the game-winning field goal in overtime.
No handshakes, no postgame pleasantries.
Just two catches for 48 yards and an immediate exit.
Considering Southern Oregon has now lost three consecutive games after starting 5-0, I imagine Mike was right behind him.
Three weeks ago, we were genuinely discussing whether anyone in the PDL could beat Southern Oregon.
Since then, Mike has lost to Delco, Greg, and now Welch.
That's a pretty incredible sequence when you consider that one of those teams is currently ranked dead last and another spent most of October actively dismantling its roster.
And Mike can't even blame Josh Allen anymore.
Allen returned from his bye, threw for 289 yards, scored three touchdowns, and passed Jim Kelly for the most touchdown passes in Bills history.
He gave Mike 29.56 points, which is about as much as you can reasonably ask from your starting quarterback.
The problem is that the other nine starters combined for 82.30.
I've been making fun of Mike's running backs for so long that I almost feel obligated to apologize to them individually.
Ollie Gordon and Ashton Jeanty were actually beginning to look promising last week, and now they're back to combining for 15.70 points.
Meanwhile, Justin Jefferson, George Pickens and Sam LaPorta combined for 24.10.
Puka Nacua continues to be his only real saving grace in that room.
Brock Purdy was on bye, which left Mike starting Zach Charbonnet in his Superflex spot.
Charbonnet contributed 4.40 points.
Daniel Jones was available on the bench, although his 6.46 would've barely made a difference.
Kenneth Gainwell and Rico Dowdle both outscored Mike's starting running backs, but even the best lineup adjustments wouldn't have saved him against Welch.
Mike has spent much of the season trying to address the running back position, but this roster was supposed to be able to survive a disappointing week from those guys.
The entire appeal of Southern Oregon was having Allen, Purdy, Puka, Jefferson, Pickens and two excellent tight ends capable of carrying the offense.
We're now watching those players have mediocre afternoons together far more frequently than I could have anticipated.
Mike scored 111.86 points against Dallas, and he's averaging just under 115 over his three-game losing streak.
For a team that opened the season looking capable of putting up 170 whenever it felt like it, that's a pretty alarming change.
I'm beginning to get flashbacks to the 2023 Philadelphia Eagles.
They started 10-1, everyone spent months arguing about how good they were, and then they completely unraveled while the rest of the league tried to figure out what happened.
At least the Eagles waited until December.
Mike managed to fit the entire experience into October.
11: Last week, I gave Brett a hard time for trading J.K. Dobbins to Hollywood for a 2029 fourth-round pick.
Seven days later, Jonah Coleman out-carried Dobbins, led Denver in receiving yards, and scored the go-ahead touchdown against Kansas City.
Sean Payton apparently agrees with Brett's assessment of the Broncos backfield, and now they are connected to JT.
Dobbins finished with seven carries for 16 yards. Coleman had 104 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown.
Meanwhile, Trevor Lawrence returned from his bye week and immediately participated in what I can only describe as the public execution of the Indianapolis Colts.
Jacksonville won 42-7, and Lawrence threw three touchdowns on TEN COMPLETIONS.
He only attempted 14 passes before leaving early in the fourth quarter.
The Colts spent the previous week trading away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, then showed up in Jacksonville and played like the remaining roster had also requested a transfer.
Unfortunately for Brett, Lawrence's return coincided with a matchup against Jeff, who remains capable of scoring 145 points regardless of what happens around him.
Dubrovnik improved considerably from last week's 68.70-point embarrassment, finishing with 108.60. That would've beaten four other teams in the PDL this week.
But Jeff scored 145.42, and Brett fell to 3-5.
I'm starting to feel a little bad about how quickly that three-game winning streak disappeared.
Brett specifically asked for recognition when he reached .500, and since receiving it, he's lost to a Delco team missing both starting quarterbacks and then to the top-ranked team in the league.
The roster is at least showing some interesting developments.
Coleman looks increasingly capable of becoming a legitimate starting running back, Kraft continues to produce, and Loveland has become a useful piece of the offense.
That's encouraging for someone who has already made it clear he's more interested in building a long-term contender than squeezing out another win in November.
But there's still a noticeable difference between the players Brett is excited about owning in three years and the ones he can actually rely on every Sunday.
Omarion Hampton managed 3.70 points, and the receiving group is still struggling to produce anything resembling a complete week together.
At 3-5, the playoff picture is getting considerably less forgiving. Brett has four future first-round picks and plenty of young talent, so there's no reason to panic about the long-term direction.
12: Jonathan Taylor carried the ball eight times for 23 yards while Indianapolis got embarrassed 42-7 by Jacksonville.
He then spent his postgame interview answering questions about whether he'd be traded.
Travis Hunter, whom Tanish started at wide receiver, caught zero passes and recorded four tackles playing cornerback.
Between them, they contributed 5.20 fantasy points.
Tanish still beat Delco by 62.54.
What's particularly upsetting is that Tanish had Jaylen Warren and Chimere Dike sitting on his bench with 20.80 and 15.60 points, respectively.
Had he started those two over Taylor and Hunter, Boulder would've finished with 178.04 points, easily leading the PDL this week.
Darren needed 167.50 to earn the highest score of the week, and Tanish had a better lineup available that would've topped him by another ten points.
Drake Maye continued his impressive season by completing 16 of 20 passes against Miami, throwing two touchdowns and rushing for another.
New England trailed 13-3 at halftime before Maye went 9-for-10 in the second half to lead the comeback.
Tanish also got another 20.80 points from Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who caught six passes for 118 yards and a touchdown against Chicago.
JSN now has seven 100-yard receiving performances through eight games.
Only three other receivers in the Super Bowl era have accomplished that, including Marvin Harrison Sr.
I appreciate the NFL finding another opportunity to remind me what a functioning member of the Harrison family looks like.
Dalton Kincaid also caught four passes for 86 yards and a touchdown against Baltimore.
The Ravens managed 68 NET passing yards in the entire game.
Tanish's tight end personally outgained Baltimore's passing offense while Josh Allen was busy dismantling whatever remains of a Ravens season that was supposed to end with a Super Bowl appearance.
And this was all with Malik Nabers on bye.
Tanish has now scored 197.72, 145.50, 151.26 and 146.84 over the past four weeks.
That's an average of 160.33 points, and we've reached November with the defending champion sitting at 7-1.
Jeff has the same record, and I'm still keeping Wichita at #1 for now.
But there's very little separating these two teams anymore.
I'd strongly recommend he keep Travis Hunter starting at receiver.
At this point, those half-point performances might be the only thing keeping Boulder from scoring 180 every Sunday.
